newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl sure joblessness will turn this year - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sure joblessness will turn this year - paper.

text.p: Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl said he was certain unemployment figures would improve this year after they hit a new post-war record of 4.66 million in January, a German newspaper reported on Thursday.
"I am sure that we can bring about a change in the trend this year," Kohl told Die Rheinpfalz daily in an interview, excerpts of which were released ahead of publication on Friday.
Kohl said the figures were the blackest of his 14-year term in office, but he was sure they would get better because the economy was picking up slowly.
He expected proposed tax and pension reforms to help boost the economy. Labour reforms to make it more attractive to hire staff would help to create 100,000 to 200,000 new jobs, he told the paper.
German unemployment surged by over a half a million to a new post-war record of 4.66 million in January. The unemployment rate rose to 12.2 percent, compared with 10.8 percent in December.
The increase, boosted by bad weather that idled large numbers of construction workers, came as a major surprise to independent analysts.
